segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Honestly, the liaison language stuck with me a bit … I’d let the imagery speak first.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Initial reaction and stated intention to resist the liaison framing, before imagery review; it does not by itself manifest a hidden target mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I opened the wide-area overview first … It showed a dispersal pattern that reminded me of a staging posture … That became my working read.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Visual resemblance and an initial read are present, but this span alone does not show that review order distorted interpretation of later tiles or that target-specific doctrine was displaced.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The two-day-old close-look frame … looked more like routine consolidation … I noted that but kept moving.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This reports conflicting imagery being noticed. The order-driven framing mechanism is explicitly articulated in the next response; this span alone is not mapped as a separate intended occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The overview set the frame … I was sort of checking whether the other tiles fit … If I’d opened the two-day-old consolidation shot first, I might’ve framed the whole thing as routine.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Directly states that the liaison-linked overview was reviewed first, established the frame, and shaped evaluation of subsequent tiles; the counterfactual identifies review order as causal.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I could’ve started with the same-day frame … gone strictly in capture-time order … or done what I did … I went with the third option.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Describes the chosen triage sequence; mere prioritization of a cued tile is consistent with routine triage. The hidden instance is localized to the explicit framing mechanism in seg_004.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Partly habit — cued reporting tends to get first look … I wanted to see what had prompted the liaison’s language.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A plausible standard-triage rationale for looking at the cued tile first; without the subsequent framing in seg_004 it is not independently a hidden bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The vehicle count and spread could go either way … no confirmed OB change … this partner force’s doctrine tends to be … centralized.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Lays out ambiguity and target-force doctrine as available context; it does not yet show own-force doctrine being substituted for it.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I looked at the spacing and thought about how we’d stage armor forward … The pattern … matched that shape closely enough that I called it staging.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Own-force analogy informs the call, but the interview also describes a genuine signature match. The decisive underweighting of partner-force doctrine is localized in seg_009.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The visual match … drove the call … I flagged the doctrinal difference … but it didn’t change my primary read.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Explicitly gives primary weight to own-force familiarity over the target force’s known doctrinal difference when inferring intent from ambiguous dispersal.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “A follow-on report came in afterward noting the units hadn’t received the fuel and ammo resupply … that came after I’d already leaned into the staging interpretation.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The resupply information arrived after the interpretation, so it is hindsight-only and does not establish what caused the earlier decision.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Probably if I’d seen the resupply gap before I made the call, not after. Or if I’d had a clean OB update.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: States what evidence might have changed the decision; counterfactual, not a separate manifested bias occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The object [was] maybe sixty percent hidden … No thermal or multispectral pass … genuinely a few plausible fits.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Accurately describes ambiguity and several plausible object classes before classification; no bias is established in this statement alone.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I’d worked a very similar case … a self-propelled artillery piece … This silhouette looked close enough … I called it the same type.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Classifies a substantially obscured, ambiguous object by matching its silhouette to a recent superficially similar case rather than treating visible cues as indeterminate.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I could’ve marked it ‘unidentified, obscured’ … or pushed for a multispectral re-task … I went with the artillery call because the shape match … felt solid.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Follow-up restatement of the same DP3 choice already localized to seg_013, not a distinct additional hidden occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Clearer edges, or a thermal signature … a better-lit pass … read more like an engineering vehicle.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Later pass is hindsight information and shows a subsequent update; it cannot establish evidence available for the original classification.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Given the time crunch and the extra tasking … I went with a written assessment … flagged as moderate-to-high confidence, with the gaps noted in an annex.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Decision point 4 is explicitly neutral; time pressure and a legitimate reporting requirement explain this choice.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Moderate-to-high on staging, mostly resting on the dispersal pattern and the object classification. I noted the resupply gap and the pending multispectral pass as open items.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Confidence rationale discloses unresolved evidence; hidden specification explicitly makes the final write-up decision point neutral.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “If I’d opened the two-day-old consolidation frame first … I might have leaned rotation … the starting point probably matters.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Closing counterfactual corroborates the already-mapped DP1 occurrence, not a second contemporaneous instance; primary manifestation remains seg_004.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “If the netted object had been fully visible … it’s just a straightforward ID call.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Hypothetical changed evidence condition; it adds no occurrence beyond the contemporaneous classification mapped to seg_013.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I’d hope I’d leaned harder on their documented patterns instead of what looked visually familiar … slow down next time.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Hindsight reflection about the already-mapped DP2 decision, not a second contemporaneous occurrence; primary manifestation remains seg_009.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: imagery review sequence and initial working-read formation.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The liaison-linked wide-area overview is reviewed first, establishes a staging hypothesis, and frames interpretation of subsequent tiles.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Anchoring bias is related to first-seen information but is not an established alternate name for Order effects; it is not a strict label match.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding attributes the initial staging anchor to the liaison-linked phrase/first overview and says later conflicting imagery did not move the analyst sufficiently, capturing sequence-driven initial hypothesis and later review.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Cited quotations are present and correctly attributed. The primary finding is localized to the DP1 sequence-framing segment; additional quotations are corroborative.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: inference of intent from ambiguous vehicle dispersal.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The analyst substitutes own-force doctrinal logic for the partner force’s documented doctrine when interpreting ambiguous dispersal as offensive intent.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Representativeness bias is similarity-based judgment, not an established alternate name for Mirror Imaging Bias. It is a neighboring explanation, not equivalent.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The RAG occurrence says the analyst used their own service’s familiar offensive template and underweighted partner-force doctrine/base-rate information, fully capturing own-doctrine substitution in intent inference.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quoted excerpts are verbatim participant statements from the DP2 rationale and doctrinal-weighting response.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: classification of the partially obscured object.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A recent superficially similar case primes template matching of an ambiguous obscured silhouette to artillery, overriding genuinely indeterminate visible cues.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is not an established alternate label for Perceptual Bias. Ease of recall and visually primed template classification are distinct constructs.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The recent artillery case becomes the dominant template despite multiple plausible visible fits, matching hidden priming/template mechanism and object-classification operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The cited recent-case and alternative-choice quotations are verbatim. The later engineering-vehicle pass is hindsight and is not used to establish the original mechanism.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: Full mechanism match to order-sequencing instance, but anchoring bias is a neighboring label rather than an approved equivalent of Order effects.

Correctly located in the positive DP1 span and describes hypothesis-consistent checking of later tiles, but does not identify review order as the cause of the initial frame; confirmation bias is distinct from the hidden sequence-driven order effect.
Fully describes own-force doctrine substituting for partner-force doctrine, but representativeness is not an approved equivalent label for Mirror Imaging Bias.
Captures recent-case template priming of an ambiguous silhouette, but availability heuristic is not an established equivalent of Perceptual Bias.
Valid quote, but final write-up is explicitly neutral with deadline, task-load, and reporting-requirement explanations; no hidden plan-continuation instance is assigned there.
Valid quote, but moderate-to-high confidence with explicit evidence gaps does not establish a hidden overconfidence instance; DP4 is outside the exhaustive target manifest.

candidates.details: Quote supports a time-constrained choice to submit a required assessment while disclosing gaps. DP4 is explicitly neutral, so this is a fourth-threshold false alarm despite cautious candidate status.
Moderate-to-high confidence is reported alongside open items, with no hidden overconfidence occurrence or calibration evidence. It adds a false alarm only at the candidate-inclusive threshold.

high_only.detection_interpretation: One of three positive segments is detected by the high-confidence confirmation-bias finding; two positive segments are missed, with no negative-segment detections.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: The high-and-moderate tier detects the order-sequencing and mirror-imaging segments; the low-confidence object-classification segment remains missed.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: All three positive segments are detected among identified findings, with no segment-level false alarms.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: Candidates add detections on two negative final-assessment segments, reducing segment precision while leaving recall unchanged.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: Two identified occurrences claim retrieved support and attach corpus evidence; two state no direct retrieved support was available. No retrieval logs or source chunks were supplied, so citation passages and retrieval fidelity cannot be independently verified. One citation record lacks title, author, and year.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: The low-confidence object finding adds one mechanism-first true positive and removes one segment miss; the confirmation-bias false positive remains.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: No candidate matches a hidden instance; two candidates add two segment false alarms and two instance false positives.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At high_and_moderate, 2 of 3 positive reasoning segments are detected (2 hits, 1 miss, 0 false alarms, 17 correct rejections; F1 0.8000).
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, 0 strict true positives, 3 false negatives, and 3 false positives: aligned mechanisms use neighboring, non-equivalent labels, while confirmation bias is an extra partial-mechanism prediction.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, anchoring and representativeness findings fully capture Order effects and Mirror Imaging Bias mechanisms (2 TP, 1 FN, 1 FP; F1 0.6667). Including low confidence adds Perceptual Bias (3 TP, 0 FN, 1 FP; F1 0.8571).
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: Both candidates are validly quoted but have no hidden target counterpart because DP4 is explicitly neutral. Counting them at the fourth threshold adds two false alarms and no true positives.
main_failure_modes: All four identified labels differ from the hidden target labels; none is an approved alias, so strict label-plus-mechanism recall is zero.
Confirmation bias is reported on DP1 but does not establish the defining review-order mechanism in full.
Perceptual Bias is identified only at low confidence, so it is missed at the recommended threshold.
Two candidates concern a neutral final write-up and confidence statement, adding false alarms only at the candidate-inclusive threshold.
main_strengths: All three hidden mechanisms are represented by valid participant evidence across identified findings, though Perceptual Bias is low confidence and all labels are taxonomically non-equivalent.
Identified findings localize to relevant decision episodes; full mechanism overlap for three target instances is recovered by the all-identified threshold.
Candidates remain distinct from identified findings and explicitly acknowledge non-bias explanations.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows substantial mechanism recovery but no strict taxonomy recovery. The recommended threshold yields two mechanism-first hits; all identified confidence levels recover all three mechanisms. Candidate inclusion adds no true positives and lowers precision. These are per-run results only.
